source: Transcribed from the Siglent SDG Series Programming Guide (PG02_E05B), which covers the whole SDG line — every SDG model classifies into this family, so the catalog is no longer held to what an SDG2000X supports. Several subsystems are model-specific and the guide says which: Sequence, Digital Channel, Frequency Hop and File Operations are SDG7000A, the :SENSe:COUNTer tree is SDG7000A (the older FreqCouNTer command is the one on other models), and IQ Modulation is SDG6000X and later. Commands are listed in the short form Siglent's own table pairs with each long one — BSWV for BaSic_WaVe — except where only the long form is documented. The channel prefix is written C<n>: here, which is this project's placeholder rather than either of the guide's: its syntax lines print <channel>: and its worked examples print C1: with a literal digit. That one substitution accounts for every entry a guide sweep reports as absent — all 200 of them are found under <channel>:, and 183 under C1: as well, so nothing in this catalog is missing from the guide, only spelled the way the rest of these catalogs spell a channel. Three more the guide's own availability tables mark as not on an SDG2000X: Comm_HeaDeR (CHDR) is SDG800/SDG1000/SDG5000 only, and KEY and POWER:ON:MODE are SDG7000A only. A bench sweep of an SDG2042X on firmware 2.01.01.17R5 got no reply at all from five the tables do mark as available on an SDG2000X — C<n>:HARM?, C<n>:CMBN?, MODE?, CURRPRT? and VOLTSTAT? — nor from C<n>:NOISE_ADD?, which the guide gives no availability table for at all. VOLTPRT? answered ON, so the two silent protection queries are not a subsystem this model lacks. Settled on 10 August 2026 by asking the instrument's own error queue: after C1:HARM? goes unanswered, SYST:ERR? returns -113,Undefined header,C1:HARM?. The firmware does not have the command, so silence is a rejection rather than a timeout or a feature switched off — and a subsystem that is merely off still answers, C1:MDWV? replying STATE,OFF. All six are therefore documented by the guide for an SDG2000X and absent from this unit's firmware, which is a gap between the two rather than an error in either. They stay transcribed as the guide has them, and none is bench-verified. Worth knowing before repeating the experiment: the SDG's VXI-11 link stops working on a query it does not understand, so every command after it reads as empty until the link is rebuilt. Rebuilding recovers it — a full sweep of all 104 sendable entries reconnected 80 times and the instrument answered *IDN? after every one — but rebuilding needs a pause. Sending a burst of unknown headers down one link with no gap took the whole SCPI service down instead, off a subnet scan entirely, until it was power-cycled. Of those 104, 24 answer; the other 80 are refused, and three more entries carry a bench tick from being driven by hand rather than read back, which is why the catalog counts 27.
